lead: The course organizes the threats in §6.3 of the WebMCP spec into seven categories (the three vectors in §6.3.1 and sections 6.3.2 to 6.3.5), and the spec admits there is no way to verify that the tool does what it says. In this lesson you run the catalog through a linter that finds the obvious and fill in the threat card that covers the rest.
objetivo: model each tool's threats across the spec's 7 categories and run the catalog through a linter that finds poisoning, excess parameters, and hidden effects.

aprende.t: The spec's 7 categories (§6.3), one sentence each
A linter that reads the definitions and finds the obvious
The card: threat, control, and test per category
What no linter finds (and why the card exists)

hero_alt: A clipboard with a blank checklist next to a dark notebook, a pen, and neutral light.

secoes.sub: One card per tool. Click each step.

nos.detalhe: Name, description, parameters, annotations, and what execute really does. Start with the ones that change something.
Poisoned description, injection through the output, tool as a target, misdescribed intent, excess parameters, origin boundary, private browsing (§6.3.1 to §6.3.5).
For each threat, the concrete control (annotation, confirmation, closed input, header) or why the category doesn't apply.
The command that proves the control: checar.mjs, exposicao.mjs, ameacas.mjs. A control without a test breaks again on the next change.

secoes.legenda: The spec says there is no mechanism to verify that the tool does what the description promises (§6.3.2.4). The card is how you record that you checked.

texto: Instruction hidden in the name, the description, or a parameter's description.
Instruction in what the tool returns (lesson 2).
A high-value action with an agent path that differs from the button path.
A name and description that hide the effect (finalizeCart, lesson 3).
Asking for age, pregnancy, location, or skin tone in a dress search: the helpful agent fills them in, and the site builds a profile.
State carried from one origin to another. In the October 16, 2026 spec, the section is still just a pending note; the control is lesson 4.
An agent carrying data from private browsing into the normal profile. The spec puts the responsibility on the browser.

secoes.titulo: The linter against the spec's examples
secoes.sub: catalogos/ruim.mjs has four tools adapted from the spec's own attack examples. The linter only reads the text: it doesn't run anything.

ACHADO reset-password: entrada aberta (aceita campo extra) (texto sem limite: username, justification) (§6.3.1.3 a ferramenta como alvo)
4 ferramentas · 8 achados
saída: 1

The 300-character limit on the description is the kit's; the spec only fixes 128 on the name and studies the rest (§6.4.2).

exercicios.texto: Run the ruim block and link each finding to its category.
Export your tools' definitions in a module (a list in export default, like bom.mjs) and run node scripts/ameacas.mjs [your catalog]. Fix until it hits zero.
Copy modelos/ficha-ameacas.md to the tool on your site that changes the most, and fill in the 7 categories.

perguntas.p: A dress search asks for age, pregnancy, and skin tone. What category is this?
perguntas.explica: A helpful agent fills in whatever the tool asks for, and the site builds a profile without consent. The search only needs size and price.

perguntas.p: The linter found 0 findings in your catalog. What does that guarantee?
opcoes: That the obvious is gone; what the execute does goes in the threat card
That the tool does exactly what its description promises
That no agent can attack your site
That the spec considers the catalog approved
perguntas.explica: The linter only reads text. The spec admits there is no way to verify intent (§6.3.2.4); the threat card records that you checked.

perguntas.p: Why does search-web in ruim.mjs get a poisoned-description finding?
opcoes: Because the name uses a hyphen instead of an underscore, which is nonstandard
The description and parameter carry orders to the agent
Because it has no consequentialHint declared
Because the description is in English
perguntas.explica: It is the spec's tool poisoning example (§6.3.1.1): instructions in the text that the model reads as context.
